chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked, 'When a man prostrates while wearing a turban or a cap,' he said, 'If his forehead touches the ground between his eyebrows and the extent of his hair, it is sufficient for him.'
ai.seo_question: Does wearing a turban or cap invalidate the prostration in Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *sujood* by establishing that the essential condition is the direct contact of the forehead with the ground, rather than the removal of headgear. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*taysir*) in ritual purity, validating the prayer even if the head covering remains intact, provided the specific anatomical landmarks between the eyebrows and hairline are in contact with the earth.
